newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian bonds seen capped by exchange auction.
newsitem.headline: Belgian bonds seen capped by exchange auction.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds, which rose on light but persistent buying in morning trading on Tuesday, are expected to be contained for the rest of the day awaiting the results of the regular OLO exchange auction, traders said.
"The market was capped this morning, waiting for the auction and is likely to remain so for the rest of the day," one said.
Traders noted that the market lagged German Bunds and added that it was likely to continue doing so.
They said that once the auction was out of the way the focus would switch to U.S. September CPI data due on Wednesday.
The Treasury is offering OLOs 11 (July 1998), 13 (April 1999), 7 (June 2001) and the new OLO 26 (March 2007) in exchange for OLOs 15 (May 1997) and eight (August 1997).
Once the auction is out of the way the focus will shift to the U.S. consumer price figures and then the German money supply data due later in the week, traders said.

They noted that the only real buying on Tuesday morning was by Generale Bank which again was seeking 2004 paper. They added that barring unforeseen events they expected the market to remain rangebound for the rest of the week.
The benchmark 2006 OLO yielded 6.06 percent at 0930 GMT down from 6.11 at Monday's close. The spread over equivalent Bunds was at nine basis points against Monday's eight.
The front-month bond futures contract was up 36 basis points at 119.73.
